newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy could seek to widen Albania mission - minister.
newsitem.headline: Italy could seek to widen Albania mission - minister.

text.p: Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta was quoted on Friday as saying that Italy could seek a wider mandate for the multinational security force it is leading in Albania so that it could help oversee planned elections.

"We want the elections to take place and we are ready also to ask for an expansion of the mandate to guarantee that they take place without incident or irregularity," Andreatta told La Stampa newspaper in an interview.

Italy is commanding a 6,000-strong force which has a three-month U.N. mandate to secure the delivery of humanitarian aid in the impoverished Balkan state following its slide towards anarchy in March after the collapse of dubious savings schemes.
But the force, whose mandate can be renewed by the United Nations, has no authority to disarm Albanians or seize thousands of weapons looted from state armouries when order collapsed.
Andreatta this week gave the first indication that the mission could be cut short if the elections failed to take place on schedule because of a dispute over a new electoral law.

Parties signed a deal on March 9 which installed Bashkim Fino of the main opposition Socialist Party as prime minister of an interim unity government and provided for an early general election to be held by the end of June.

The election plan has since run into deep trouble over a failure between parties to agree on the voting system and rules. Albania's last election, in 1996, was criticised internationally as irregular and was boycotted by the Socialists.
"I confirm that if the Fino government falls, we will withdraw the mission," Andreatta told La Stampa.
"We are working so that it does not fall, clearly, but the political impasse in Albania is worrying," he said.
Mediator Franz Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, was making a final effort on Friday to resolve the deadlock between Albanian parties.
Fino was due to travel to the United States on Saturday, where he will meet Secretary of State Madeleine Albright during his five-day stay.
He plans to stop off in Rome on the way for talks on Saturday morning with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.

Italian diplomatic sources said it was too early to say whether the mission's mandate ought to be broadened. "We want to see the outcome of Vranitzky's meetings and Fino's meetings tomorrow in Rome," one source said.
